t: A small 3D-printed robot arm with six servos for classrooms.
steps: Download the parts files and parts list from the poppy-ergo-jr repo on GitHub.
Buy a Pixl board from Generation Robots and six XL-320 servos from a robot parts store.
Get a Raspberry Pi 2 or 3 Model B, a Pi camera, an 8 GB microSD card, and a 7.5 V 2 A power supply.
3D print the arm parts and print or laser cut the base.
Flash the Poppy image to the microSD card.
Assemble the arm with the plastic rivets. Plan on three to four hours.
Power on and open the Snap! editor in a web browser on the same network.
Try a first block program that moves one servo.
